chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Prostration is performed on what the earth produces, except that which is eaten or worn.'

key_terms.أَوْ لُبِسَ: Or worn (clothing/textile items, thus excluded from being used for prostration)
key_terms.السُّجُودُ: Prostration (the act of bowing the forehead to the ground in prayer)
key_terms.مَا أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ: What the earth produces (natural, edible, or wearable items from the earth)
key_terms.مَا أُكِلَ: That which is eaten (food items, thus excluded from being used for prostration)

ai.seo_question: What surfaces are permissible for prostration in Shia Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of prostrating on various natural materials, a key issue in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of prayer surfaces. It distinguishes between earth's produce that is edible or wearable—which are excluded due to their utility or value—and other natural items, reflecting the principle of using humble, non-consumable earth elements for worship.
